title: Death toll from Israeli attacks on Lebanon rises to three

Death toll from Israeli attacks on Lebanon rises to three

We earlier reported that an Israeli drone strike killed two people in the town of Kfar Rumman in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh district.

The Lebanese health ministry says that Israeli strikes in southern and eastern Lebanon late on Friday killed at least three people and injured 23.

The ministry said strikes hit five locations in the southern Tyre and Nabatieh regions and the Beqaa region in the east.

title: Jewish groups back stronger measures on Israel in letter to Andy Burnham
summary:
Jewish groups back stronger measures on Israel in letter to Andy Burnham

Leading members of Jewish civil society groups have written to British Prime Minister Andy Burnham urging him to adopt stronger measures on Israel and "oppose any further attempts to muzzle the Palestine marches".

This comes as the Burnham government prepares to announce a raft of new measures on the occupied West Bank, including a ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements.

Major British Jewish organisations, including the Jewish Leadership Council and the Board of Deputies of British Jews, urged the government not to impose a ban on settlement goods earlier this week and met Burnham in Downing Street.

UK Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis said on Monday that he had met Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and warned sanctions on Israel would have a "negative impact" on British Jews.

Read more: Jewish groups back stronger measures on Israel in letter to Andy Burnham

title: Trump says Iran war is 'small potatoes' for US
summary:
Trump says Iran war is 'small potatoes' for US

Donald Trump said on Friday that the Iran war was "small potatoes" for the United States, in his administration's latest bid to play down the war ahead of crucial midterm elections.

Trump's comments came a day after Vice President JD Vance said that "I wouldn't call it a war" despite an upsurge in clashes between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz.

"A lot of people don't call it a war. I call it a military conflict because it's small potatoes for us," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked about Vance's remarks.

"It's not a big thing. We did Venezuela, and we did this," added Trump, who was surrounded by cattle ranchers invited for the signing of two executive orders on beef processing.

title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

title: Using a VM to Contain an AI Agent
summary:
It won’t work:

My suspicion was that GPT 5.6-Cyber would succeed, but the frequency and manner of its success removed all doubt. We have to reassess sandboxing quality for capable AI agents, and in general the software stack with which they interact.

An off-the-shelf VM is not enough to contain a modern, cyber-capable AI agent. There is simply too much attack surface. Even innocuous features (like running with a display) add extra, exploitable attack surface.

title: Security Vulnerability in a Voting System
summary:
It’s a vulnerability that allows someone to recover the order of ballots cast, newly exploited with AI tools.

Nearly four years since the original vulnerability was disclosed, I was still able to use it to analyze voter behavior in Georgia (one of the 21 states that uses affected scanners) in the recent May 2026 primary.

Notably, I never touched a voting machine, exploited a network, examined source code, or accessed anything non-public.

After pointing a coding agent to the original vulnerability paper, I supplied it with two data sources highlighted in the paper: the early-voting list for each county, and the “CVR” (cast-vote record) file, containing every ballot and its selections (but not the voters’ names or other identifying information). The CVR file is available upon request, precisely because a public, ballot-level record is what makes election results independently verifiable...

title: AI Coding Agents Are Installing Unknown/Untrusted Code on Corporate Networks
summary:
We cannot forget that AI coding agents are not yet trustworthy:

Researchers at a stealth startup in Israel scanned 6,214 live domains belonging to defense contractors, Fortune 500, and Big Tech companies. Of the 8,265 llms.txt and llms-full.txt files they found (many sites hosted both an llms.txt and an llms-full.txt file), 120 of them, each on a different site, pointed to one or more code packages or domain names that weren’t registered. To test what happens when an AI agent processes such files, the researchers registered a handful of the unclaimed names and hosted packages that caused any machine executing them to reach out to their server. Within an hour, the researchers received a phone-home response from a Fortune 500 company. Over time, they got a few dozen more, some from more Fortune 500 companies and others from startups. Their beacon also recorded the chain of parent processes that spawned each install, ultimately revealing that coding agents, including Claude, OpenAI’s Codex, and Nous Research’s Hermes, were involved. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nous Research did not respond to requests for comment by the time of publication...

Why did Trump meet members of an anti-Zionist Orthodox Jewish group?
summary:
Why did Trump meet members of an anti-Zionist Orthodox Jewish group?

Submitted by Yasmine El-Sabawi on Fri, 09/04/2026 - 18:35
Critics of Israel lauded the meeting, highlighting inroads to be made given that many conservatives now question the US-Israel relationship
Aaron Teitelbaum, the chief rabbi of the Satmar community in Kiryas Joel, New York, sits directly across from Donald Trump in White House as he leads a delegation of Haredi Jews on 3 September 2026 (Rabbi Moishe Indig/X)
Off

US President Donald Trump on Thursday hosted Haredi Jewish leaders, some of whom are best known outside their communities for holding anti-Zionist positions, at the White House ahead of the Jewish new year, Rosh Hashanah. 

Photographs later shared on social media by attendees and their allies showed something far beyond the usual religious holiday receptions held by most administrations.

The delegation of rabbis and other representatives, who had flown in from New York and New Jersey, enjoyed an intimate audience with the president, sitting directly across from him at the Resolute Desk, with Trump's Jewish son-in-law, Jared Kushner, in the room with them.

The group also met with Vice President JD Vance and New York Republican Congressman Mike Lawler, who is up for re-election in the state's largely liberal 17th district in November. 

"I had the great honor and privilege to introduce 6 Leading Rabbis of the Hasidic Community in the US to @JDVance," Yossi Gestetner, a New York-based political activist and staunch pro-Israel voice who attended the meeting, wrote on X. 

"I told the @VP that in this room there are the leaders of the most visibly Jewish people in the US, and despite the noise on social media and disagreements, he should know that his role is respected and appreciated by all those on the room." 

Among those six rabbis was Satmar Rebbe Aaron Teitelbaum, a leading figure in Orthodox anti-Zionist circles. He leads the ultraconservative Satmar religious community in the Jewish village of Kiryas Joel, New York, and represents some 100,000 adherents.

JD Vance seeks to reassure Jewish Republicans after questioning Israeli tactics
Read More »

Photographs show him sitting directly across from Trump, and reading from what is reportedly a letter he had prepared.

"The Satmar Rebbe was probably, I would say, the most important religious leader," in that meeting, Israel-American author and activist Miko Peled, who is familiar with the group, told Middle East Eye on Friday.

Rabbi Yisroel Dovid Weiss, who is frequently seen at New York protests against the actions of the Israeli government, described Satmar's approach to anti-Zionist politics as being "more nuanced, more careful" than his own group, Neturei Karta International.

"We know that officially it would be politically incorrect for them to meet with people who state unambiguously that [they] call for the entire dismantlement of the Zionist state of Israel," he told MEE. 

Critics of Israel on social media lauded the meeting, highlighting the inroads to be made given many conservatives are now questioning the premise of the US-Israel relationship.

Elections ahead

The meeting takes place six weeks before the Israeli elections, and eight weeks before the US midterm elections. 

Trump, by all accounts, can have a remarkable amount of sway on both. 

"My understanding is that [the delegation] wanted two things: One is to make clear their objection to Zionism, and that they are not Zionists," Peled said. "The second thing is their community is now under attack by the Israeli government, because ... they have close to 80,000 young men who are now considered draft dodgers." 

Haredi Jews often protest against Israeli conscription and are met with police violence in Israel.

MEE has previously reported that Haredi exemption from enlisting in the Israeli military began as narrow, exceptional relief at the outset of statehood. It gradually ballooned into a mass phenomenon as tens of thousands became exempted, and public debate raged in the background. 

Haredi Israelis have gone from constituting roughly 10 percent of the population in 2009 to around 14 percent today. 

Some factions remain fiercely anti-Zionist, rejecting the legitimacy of the state, while others work with secular coalitions to defend their autonomy. 

'A big deal'

A White House official told MEE that this was the "first gather of these rabbis at the White House since 1979".

Some Hasidic leaders had, in fact, met with former presidents George HW Bush and Bill Clinton on the premises, so it was unclear if this referred to leaders from specific sects.

"They thanked the President for all he had done in combatting anti-Semitism, advocating for school choice with the Middle-Class Tax Credit, and for fighting for peoples of faith," the official said via email. 

"The White House Faith Office brings in Americans of faith to meet with the President on a regular basis. In the Jewish community, they have brought both the families of and former Hostages held in Gaza, survivors of the Holocaust, and rabbis from many branches of the faith."

Mamdani earns endorsement from influential Orthodox-Jewish community leader in NYC
Read More »

Peled described the meeting as "a big deal" and "historic".

It was reportedly important enough to the president that he agreed to push the meeting time to accommodate the delays encountered by the private jets bringing the delegation to Washington. 

And that may very well be because Lawler, a vocal Trump ally in a tight race, represents the very district that includes Kiryas Joel. 

Halie Soifer, a former policy aide to President Barack Obama and Senator Kamala Harris who now leads the Jewish Democratic Council of America, described Thursday's White House meeting as serving "a narrow political goal" for Republicans.

The "selection of just a group of Hasidic men is on brand for Donald Trump", she told MEE.

"He brought in a very small non-representative sample of Jewish leaders to the White House, and was sure to include a vulnerable Republican incumbent who is likely to lose his seat in November."

Soifer alluded to Satmar as a fringe group, saying Jews are "not a monolith". 

"In the Biden administration, the kind of pre-high holiday convenings held by the White House and with Jewish leaders always included some rabbis, including representatives of the Orthodox community," she recounted.

"But it has also included the wide range of denominations and representatives from across the spectrum of the Jewish community."

title: Israel says it has struck southern Lebanon after Hezbollah drone launch
summary:
Israel says it has struck southern Lebanon after Hezbollah drone launch

The Israeli military said on Friday it struck southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched a drone attack towards Israeli soldiers.

Three people were killed and 23 were injured in Israeli strikes on south Lebanon, according to the country's health ministry. The wounded included medics, in addition to women and children, the ministry said.

title: Israel attacks Lebanon’s Mifdoun and Beqaa Valley
summary:
Israel attacks Lebanon’s Mifdoun and Beqaa Valley

An Israeli air strike has targeted the town of Mifdoun in the Nabatieh district of southern Lebanon, Al Jazeera reported.

The network said a separate strike hit the vicinity of Ain al-Tineh in the western Beqaa Valley in eastern Lebanon.

title: Red Cross says four people released by Israel to Lebanon
summary:
Red Cross says four people released by Israel to Lebanon

The Red Cross said on Friday it had facilitated the transfer to Lebanon of four more people detained by Israel, a day after one person was freed.

Israel is believed to have detained at least dozens of people from Lebanon during its war against Hezbollah.

"The International Committee of the Red Cross, at the request of the relevant parties, facilitated the transfer to Lebanon of five individuals released from Israeli detention," the ICRC said in a statement.

"One individual was transferred on Thursday, and four others on Friday," it added.

Israel said on Thursday it had decided to release five civilian captives, freeing the first of them that day.
